doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: More names in the lineage: Lou Levy, Brad Mehldau, Victor Feldman and Danilo Perez
summary: Prompted by Williams she adds Lou Levy, Stanley Cowell, Stephen Scott, Brad Mehldau, Paul Bley, Victor Feldman, Danilo Perez, Cyrus Chestnut and Hank Jones.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now once again, what about as we get . . . You mentioned some in the ’50s. As we get to the ’60s, ’70s, ’80s, ’90s. Are there any names that you want to say that would be in that lineage that you’ve . . .
God, so many . . .
Well, just a few. We don’t have to have a . . .
But I can’t come up with them. How old would they be now? Would we be thinking of guys . . .
Be anywhere . . .
. . . in their seventies, like Lou Levy?
He would probably be one that would . . .

Or Stanley Cowell? Definitely. I mentioned Hampton Hawes. Red Garland. My God, everybody aped that style for a while, his playing. Well, now I’m going back to old guys again. I should . . . I’m trying to get the middle road. Then I keep thinking of guys like Stephen Scott, and the guy that’s working with Joshua Redman. The guy that’s working with Joshua Redman is Brad Mehldau.
Would someone like Paul Bley fall into line there, you feel?
Yes he would. Mention a few names to me. Now Paul Bley’s somebody . . . Carla Bley is . . .
Victor Feldman.
I thought Victor Feldman was fantastic. I’m glad you’re mentioning these people, because he went and died when he shouldn’t have died. What’s that thing he wrote?
“Joshua.”
No.
“Seven Steps to Heaven.”
He wrote a marvelous piece that everybody plays.
“Seven Steps to Heaven.”
“Seven Steps to Heaven.” Yeah. Marvelous. Love that piece.
That gives us a little idea.
God, I haven’t come up with any Latin names. There’s a couple of guys who now are so terrific. From Boston. I can’t think of his name. Had him on “Piano Jazz.”
Danilo Pérez.
Yes, Danilo.
He was a student of Donald Brown, are you aware?
Was he?
Yeah, he and Cyrus Chestnut, at Berklee.
There’s another one, Cyrus Chestnut.
We’re out of the Donald Brown school of studies. [laughs]
Of course we’re going to the old guys now. Hank Jones.
Hank was a little before you, though.
Oh yes. He definitely was. I switched generations. That’s more my generation.
